body:
If FIPS-140 compliance is required, use PBKDF2 with a work factor of 310,000 or more and set with an internal hash function of HMAC-SHA-256.

https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html

[2.4.3 Verify that if PBKDF2 is used, the iteration count SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, typically at least 100,000 iterations.](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#:~:text=verify%20that%20if%20pbkdf2%20is%20used%2C%20the%20iteration%20count%20should%20be%20as%20large%20as%20verification%20server%20performance%20will%20allow%2C%20typically%20at%20least%20100%2C000%20iterations.)

| pbkdf2 | time  |
|--------|-------|
| 100000 | 25 ms |
| 200000 | 50 ms |
| 300000 | 75 ms |
| 310000 | 76 ms |

@jmanico, do you have more information on what 310,000 was based on?

This is from one of the hashcat team leads who helped write the recent update to:

https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html

Jim Manico

can we round up to 400k or more?

I would prefer not to exclude older hardware of legacy apps since [SP 800-132 Recommendation for Password-Based Key Derivation: Part 1: Storage Applications](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-132/final) does not specify the work factor for PBKDF2 but can still be verified (i.e. the work factor).

I'd support a fork of ASVS adhering to the [Password Storage Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html) too.
The change is already live and consistent with the password storage cheetsheet so closing out for now

> The change is already live and consistent with the password storage cheetsheet so closing out for now

I believe this change needs additional approval from other Project Leaders otherwise it appears to be a conflict of interest and is also not aligned to SP 800-132.

Can you be more specific as to how the ASVS conflicts with SP 800-132? Jim said

> internal hash function of HMAC-SHA-256.

and SP 800-132 says:

> This Recommendation approves PBKDF2 as the PBKDF using HMAC with any approved hash function as the PRF.

So this doesn't seem to conflict.

On the work factor, SP 800-132 says:

> A minimum iteration count of 1,000 is recommended.

But this is really a theoretical minimum and they encourage you to increase this so the hashing takes several seconds. So I think the ASVS and SP 800-132 do not necessarily disagree. What do you think, @cmlh?

I worked with the hashcat team and math to come up these recommendations and I stand by them. Most standards that cite how to use PBKDF2 are wrong and I’m standing by this rather extensive work to come up with these values. Thanks.
Do you have notes of your meeting with the hashcat team? Can we view the math you used somewhere?

My core issue by excluding legacy hardware that can only support the "_...minimum iteration count of 1,000_" then these well intended changes can have unintended consequences similar to that of https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/issues/5771

I would have preferred we socialized the changes upstream with NIST against [SP 800-132 Recommendation for Password-Based Key Derivation: Part 1: Storage Applications](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-132/final) [if we haven't already] and then merge the ASVS Fork of the recently updated [Password Storage Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html).
